nl.title: User xxxx has used up –% of their bandwidth and –% of his/her allocated disk space
nl.excerpt: Betekenis van “used up X% bandwidth/disk” mails en wat je moet doen.
nl.bodyHtml:
DirectAdmin stuurt usage-warnings vóór harde limieten. Handel vóór 100%.

Voorbereiding

  • Welke resource: disk of bandwidth

Stappen

  1. Open usage-grafieken in DA
  2. Ruim disk of reduceer traffic
  3. Plan upgrade als trend structureel is
  4. Bevestig dat cron/backups niet exploderen

Controleren

  • Percentage daalt of stabiliseert

Tip: Negeer 80–90% warnings niet in piekmaanden.

Let op: Reseller: check welke user de piek veroorzaakt.

Kom je er na deze stappen niet uit? Open een ticket bij TripleZero iT via het klantenpanel. Vermeld hostname, DirectAdmin-gebruikersnaam (geen wachtwoord), domein en wat je al probeerde.

Gerelateerd: bandwidth; disk-usage-da.

en.title: User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space
en.excerpt: User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space: DirectAdmin — correct module, change, test outside the panel.
en.bodyHtml:
“User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space” is done in DirectAdmin. Use the module for the task: Account Manager, Email Accounts, DNS Management, File Manager, Installatron, SSL Certificates, Cron Jobs or MySQL Management.

Preparation

  • DirectAdmin login
  • Correct domain/user
  • Backup for risky changes

Steps

  1. Sign in to DirectAdmin and select the correct account/domain.
  2. Open the relevant module (Email, DNS, File Manager, Installatron, SSL, Cron Jobs or MySQL).
  3. Note the current value or status.
  4. Apply the change and save.
  5. Test outside DirectAdmin: browser, webmail, DNS lookup or cron log.

Verify

  • Expected outcome visible outside DirectAdmin

Tip: Stay on one domain until the task is done.

Note: Changes under the wrong user account hit the wrong site.

Still stuck? Open a ticket with TripleZero iT via the client panel. Include your domain name, what you already tried, and any exact error messages (text or screenshot).

Related: Backups, SSL, email, DNS.
